Senses.Explanation: ‘Old Master Wang’ is Nanquan Puyuan’s recurrent self-designation and the label under which later records quote him. Literally, Wang, old master or teacher. In the Chan record this is Nanquan Puyuan's recurrent self-designation and the label later writers use when quoting or commenting on him. The compound occurs 760 times in 193 allowlisted texts. Nanquan's biography identifies him as Puyuan, a son of the Wang family of Zhengzhou, and immediately records him saying, 'Old Master Wang is selling himself; is there anyone who will buy?' Other self-references include the water-buffalo saying, 'Old Master Wang has raised a water buffalo since he was young,' asking Zhaozhou, 'Where is Old Master Wang at fault?' and saying that Old Master Wang, unlike Mazu, does not say 'mind is buddha' but 'not mind, not buddha, not a thing.' Later comments preserve the title while explicitly naming Nanquan.
Senses.Note: This is a person-title, not a generic entry for every teacher surnamed Wang. The explicit biography and repeated Nanquan section headings fix its principal referent. The full name 'Nanquan Old Master Wang' occurs 17 times in 12 texts; the selling-himself phrase occurs 41 times in 37.
